title: Base QA Generation V2.2.1 Discovery and reusable answer contracts
description: Offline structural contract. Root validates Discovery; reusable $defs validate TARGET, candidate, answers and blind response. JSON Schema proves neither source entailment, query uniqueness/necessity, source approval, reviewer isolation, measured difficulty nor real question diversity.

evidence.description: Exact quoted evidence bound to original source through turn_ref. Provenance and source/scene mapping are resolved against the supplied immutable source, not inferred from this object.

source_scan_row.description: All visible source turns must occur exactly once across the scan. Cross-row completeness is checked by code, not by this schema.

event.description: Legacy-compatible event ledger. Identity, temporal, quantity, and state claims require semantic source review; matching labels do not establish same-event identity.

bridge.description: A proposed source-supported identity or constraint bridge. Cross-scene support and indispensability are separately checked; the presence of these fields proves neither.

operation_node.description: Operation kinds are diagnostic labels, not difficulty evidence. High-order operations require a source-supported bridge and a supported executable rule with matching computed result; unsupported forms remain UNRESOLVED. Even successful execution does not establish source entailment or semantic difficulty.

dependency_graph.description: Proposed AND/OR dependency graph. Node identity, acyclicity, source quotation, all known alternatives, and answer binding are checked separately. Exact path enumeration is only relative to this graph.

counterpath.description: A credible actual-visible route or competing interpretation. Context-only source may lower answerability difficulty without gaining formal-evidence permission. An unresolved route blocks an optimistic hard-target decision.

path_audit.description: Bounded full-visible-source search record, not a certificate of exhaustive semantic entailment.

query_path_audit.description: Accepted candidate audit. form_sha256 uses candidate_form_fingerprint over question_type, question, options and every semantic_value. Old question/options hashes remain. Runtime checks hashes, query necessity, minimum routes and all alternatives; failed findings are retained as HOLD.

coverage_check.description: A bounded checked range for one relation family. no_candidate and not_checked are distinct; this record does not establish exhaustive discovery.

relation.description: All original relation hypotheses remain in Discovery. MODELED (or omitted representation_status) requires the supported dependency/path representation. UNSUPPORTED retains legacy identity/evidence fields and the original unsupported graph/audit if present, requires HOLD/REJECT plus a nonempty reason, and is never a hard-target proposal. It is diagnostic rather than a whole-run representation failure. V2.2.1 requires a query from Discovery onward. Modeled queries satisfy the executable contract; UNSUPPORTED cards retain a proposed query object and remain unselectable.

target.description: Pre-construction V2.2.1 TARGET. Query must exactly match selected Discovery, semantic_answer must equal executed unique query, and runtime preserves source/selection bindings, graph/certificate parity, query-specific necessity and weakest-route L3/L4. Schema grants no QA admission.

symbolic_constraint.description: Source-extracted implication or prohibited assignment. Executable support and exact value types are validated by the core rule evaluator; extraction is still a semantic hypothesis.

symbolic_value.description: Optional author-extracted symbolic proposition, bound to the fact quotation. Extra/unsupported semantic forms may be retained diagnostically but cannot be promoted merely because this object is present. Semantic entailment is not verified by JSON Schema.

executable_rule.description: A supported offline rule over source-extracted symbolic inputs. The implementation must execute the rule and require exact expected_result equality. This validates a symbolic derivation, not source entailment, exhaustive relation discovery, formal authorization, or empirical difficulty.

json_value.description: Raw JSON value; typed equality, set/relation canonicalization and finite-number restrictions are enforced in Python.

query.description: Information need frozen from Discovery into TARGET. Runtime validates actual query result, quantified semantics, uniqueness, necessary dependencies and source faithfulness. Ambiguous factual results are HOLD.

value.description: Typed set uniqueness is checked by Python typed JSON comparison; JSON Schema numeric equality would conflate 1 and 1.0.

semantic_answer.description: Semantic value independent of options/labels. Sequence order matters; sets ignore order; relation sets normalize by reachability. Python checks typed duplicates/cycles and distinguishes booleans from numbers.

task_answer.description: Answer over stable option IDs, or the same structure over frozen display labels for independent_answer. Runtime checks namespace membership, complete-order coverage, cycles, mapping and semantics.

candidate.description: Complete candidate shape, not QA PASS. Python additionally validates option/analysis coverage, evidence/status/distractor paths, semantic uniqueness/derivation, target equality, numeric/order checks, L3/L4, source eligibility and frozen mapping.

blind_response.description: Strict same-model blind output. Parser retains exact bytes, rejects duplicates/extra fields, validates labels, evidence and frozen mapping/receipt. Parse failure never repairs answers, injects Gold or triggers retry-until-agreement.

deterministic_check.description: Exact rational computation targets semantic_answer.value through semantic_path, not a legacy answer_index. Runtime verifies source-bound facts, operation, units and complete typed numeric coverage.
